newsitem.title: CANADA: IPL asks shippers to boost oil deliveries.
newsitem.headline: IPL asks shippers to boost oil deliveries.

text.p: IPL Energy Inc unit Interprovincial Pipe Line said it was asking its Canadian shippers to deliver more crude oil to the pipeline system as it operates under the rates that were expected.

IPL said on Friday that receipts at Edmonton were short 7,200 cubic metres (45,287 barrels) per day and volumes at Cromer, Manitoba were down 6,700 cubic metres (42,142 barrels) per day from what was nominated for February.
The company said it requested "shippers, if at all possible, and feeder pipelines to maximize volumes into our system."

One Calgary-based trader said he believed that many producers, faced with a wide differential between Canadian heavy crudes, like Lloydminster, and West Texas Intermediate were choosing to store volumes until spreads traditionally narrow in the spring.
The diffferential between Lloydminster and WTI was pegged at about US$6.50 per barrel.
He also said that production may have been affected by frigid western Canadian weather in the early part of the year.
